features.description: A party asks to close their account; ops review the case and decide.
A person asks to be erased; the DPO approves, refuses or executes, and the number is tombstoned.
Advertiser accounts: the party's own read, the console directory, eligibility, KYC, activity, agreements, the QR grant to an agent.
The brands an advertiser books under.
The demand-side funnel: advertisers by activation stage.
The advertiser wallet (Lot B): balance, statement, top-ups, goodwill, holds, refund requests and the finance desks over them.
Certification earned by the curriculum, listed and revoked by ops.
The agent's balance and transaction list on the phone.
Visits dispatched, accepted, scheduled, started and completed; the day view.
DR 01: the agent's home — the dashboard, the persona tabs, the offer sheet and the order cards.
The leaderboard, for the agent and for ops.
Leads near the agent, contact / visit / convert, the transactional import.
Gamification milestones: templates, targets, rewards and claims.
Agent profiles: the agent's own read and rating, the console directory and edits.
The tier ladder, an agent's tier and the acknowledgement of a move.
Training resources, modules, progress and the quiz.
What work an agent takes, and where.
A drafted listing description and the quota behind it.
An admin invite is opened and accepted here; it is minted under users.admin-invites.
Lot K2: an authenticator app (RFC 6238 TOTP) as the console second factor: enrol, confirm, disable, recovery codes, the status read; the sign-in half rides on auth.two-factor.
Lot F (Q18): the sign-in number moves in two codes, the old number first.
Sign in with Google on the user app.
OTP sign-in by SMS or email for both phone apps, refresh and logout — the door everything else is behind.
Password sign-in, forgot / reset / change password — the console door.
The console's second factor: a code sent and verified at sign-in.
Campaign analytics: digital interactions per campaign and across the book (Q109).
Campaigns: draft, inventory, spots, review, submit for payment, authorise, cancel; the lifecycle job that moves them SCHEDULED → LIVE → ENDED.
Lot D (Q44/Q120/Q138): creatives in review, the desk, the ADX-design tap-accept, the hard gate on print.
Lot E (Q7/Q106): the AI-drafted landing page, its builder, the review list, the public page and its beacon.
A campaign may target more than one market (Q8): allowed, warned against. Off: a second market is refused 409 FEATURE_OFF.
Lot B (Q41): a cancelled campaign's refund, released or rejected by finance.

Tracking codes and their QR images (QR-1: drawn by the QR engine, hosted on GenQR in front of /t/, the SVG for print, the sync for codes issued while the engine was down), the scan redirect on the hoarding, redemptions.
Announcements drafted, previewed per channel, sent now or at a time, cancelled; the job that fans them out.
The masked delivery log, a resend, and the CSV export.
The sender job: renders and sends every queued delivery on its rail, three attempts, and the rails' delivery-report webhooks.
The notification feed, read marks and the per-channel preferences.
G6 (Q103/133): the device registry under /users/me/devices and the dispatcher's push rail. Off: a phone cannot register a token and the routes answer 503 FEATURE_OFF.
The outbound templates, the events catalogue and the SMS kinds.
The unsubscribe link at the foot of every email.
Q115: the console's analytics — earnings, spend, commissions and onboarding as separate series, every one sortable and filterable.
Q116: bookings by day and by slot — digital signage and billboards carry slotsTotal, a static wall is one.
Lot U: the format guide — one JSON per import kind on the platform (columns, rules, sample rows) and a template.csv per kind, derived from the validators.

Lot U: a publisher's spots and rate card imported on their behalf — validate with a per-row plan (geocoding, the vocabulary, the ADX floor, 25 m duplicates), commit under one supply attempt or through the listing's own rate door, revoke, report.csv. ADMIN, or the publisher's agent under the listing act rule.
The dashboard aggregates across campaigns, sales, the ledger and the parties.
Lot S: the legacy-book import for advertisers, agents, print partners and employees — validate with a per-row report, commit through each party's own creation service, revoke, report.csv.
The overview tab of each user section — tiles, series, breakdowns and top tens over a window, with the previous window beside every figure.
The console's finance root: every desk under /finance not claimed by a narrower feature (rails, limits, tax rates).
ADX's invoices to advertisers, publishers' invoices to ADX, the legal entity behind them.
The ledger read, the verify walk and a reversal by finance.
Bank statement profiles, imports, lines, auto-match and the manual matches.
The monthly payment advice per wallet, generated by the job and read back as PDF.
Every credit and debit on every wallet — publisher, agent, advertiser, print partner. Metadata only: the primitives take no flag, and off would mean stopping money, which is a deploy, not a switch.
The console's read over every wallet and its entries.

Lot V: the all-India geography catalogue (GeoNames), the city rollout stages and their six function switches, the readiness read, the bulk rollout, the seed, and the hourly wind-down of a withdrawn city. Lot X-B: the city key on every party table, and the unresolved typed strings the console folds in. Lot X-L: the city key backfill from the console. Y-B: the city audience profile, the blend of both audience vendors over the city spots.
Q122: departments as a full model — the register, its members and region / work mode / employment type per employee.
The employee register: create, read, edit, remove — ADMIN at every route.
The year's holidays, seeded at boot, editable by ops; the schedule reads them.
The people registry: staff and agents in one list, no table of its own.
Schedule entries for staff and agents, with the field overlay and the audit trail read back.
Advertiser KYC: submitted on the phone, reviewed per document on the desk.
Agent KYC, reviewed by ops.

Lot N (14 Sep 2026): KYC from the desk — requested from the console (Digio on the party's behalf, or a notice to come by), recorded at the desk on their behalf, and the person's presence attested by the admin who met them. N3-B: the one-click Digio request on every party — agents and employees included.

Digio as the KYC provider: initiate, status, restart, the webhook, and the five-minute probe that moves DIGIO ↔ DEGRADED. Off: every initiate answers 503 KYC_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE and the desk works MANUAL.
Employee KYC, reviewed by ops.
Q127: a KYC case escalates from age past N x SLA, a fraud link or a reviewer's flag — assisting the reviewer, never deciding.
Q127: verified identity images and liveness videos purged after the retention window.
Lot D (Q131): the liveness video every person records once.
Agreement templates (draft / live / superseded), acceptances per party and per transaction, the stale-terms report.
Legal documents: read by kind without a token, managed and activated by ops.
The advertiser's discovery: browse, detail, similar spots, the content categories.
A publisher's listings: create, edit, submit, the content rules, the console list.
E10-2: the LISTING_REPRICED_BY_FACTOR rows shaped for the Pricing tab.
The listing review queue: read, send back, publish.
Lot D (Q5): an advertiser saves a spot and reads the shortlist back.
E11-2: the public spot page a shared link opens, metered by IP.
Lot E: the advisory rate on the publisher's own listing, and taking it.
Publishers may opt a listing into automatic acceptance (Q6): allowed, not recommended. Off: the switch, the filter and the bolt chip are not drawn, and an instant order is refused 409 FEATURE_OFF.
Reviews of a spot and of an agent, the eligibility read, the console desk that hides with a reason.
A party grants an agent PROFILE or LISTING access by QR; the grant is live, revocable and logged.
The flow templates the intake form runs on.
DR 08: the unified onboarding ladder — account type, party, the captured steps, Digio, the agreement and the status screen; the same flow for a publisher and an advertiser.
Mint, render, resolve and delete QR codes; the scan log behind them.
Onboarding submissions for every user type; an APPROVED one provisions the profile.
The agent's job: offers, accept / reject, slots, prints pickup, check-in, condition and installation capture, OTP handover, live location and evidence; the 25-minute acceptance window.
Placing an order, the publisher accepting or rejecting it, the slot negotiation, and the timers that expire an unanswered offer.
Milestone templates and plans on the console; the agent's milestone offers, scheduling, start and completion.
Ops over an order: assign or reassign the agent, approve, cancel, end the campaign, mark print-ready, and act for a publisher who is not on the phone.
The publisher installs the creative themselves: collect prints, capture condition, check in, capture installation.
The package catalogue: plans per tier and the add-ons, ADMIN and audited.
The payment link sent by SMS — public, tokenised, short by design.
Package quotes and sales: create, resend, cancel, accept terms, pay or record a payment; the active entitlements; Lot J2: free trials, the auto-renew switch and the daily renewal sweep.
Lot H (Q147): the print partner's own floor — profile and rate card, the assigned jobs walked to handover by scan, the wallet, withdrawals, payout methods and the monthly invoice.

Lot H (Q147): quote requests on an order print — ops invite the partners in reach, partners quote until the deadline, the lowest is awarded unless ops override with a note; the nightly expiry re-invites once. G13-B: the desk's list across orders.
Cashfree in test mode until its credentials arrive (Q110).
CCAvenue in test mode until its credentials arrive (Q110).
Payment intents and their status across every gateway; the console's payment list and an advertiser's payments.
Razorpay, live first: the checkout page in the system browser, the return page, the confirm and the webhook.
A refund to the original method, raised by finance and settled by the gateway.
Lot B (Q85/Q140): payout batches — drafted, submitted, approved (reserves), released (debits), exported, line by line.
Lot B (B1): every live spot accrues daily — gross = rate × quantity, commission from the stamp; the run and the quantity backfill.
Agent incentives and the rates behind them; credited or rejected by finance.
Payout methods and the IFSC lookup; verified or rejected by finance; ADX's own bank accounts.
A publisher's or agent's wallet on the phone: balance, entries, earnings, incentives.
Withdrawal requests: raised and cancelled on the phone, approved / rejected / marked paid / failed by finance, raised on a partner's behalf.
Liveness and readiness: Postgres and Redis pinged, the failing part named.
Geocoding, reverse geocoding, place search and place detail through the Maps key.
Uploading a file and reading a private one back through the one door.
Lot E (Q125): pricing factors in ADVISORY or BINDING mode; a binding apply reprices within maxBindingChangePct or raises a price case.
The city table and its per-city settings.
The evaluation, comparables, the price indicator on a listing, and the pricing settings.
Market data imports and their revocation.
Price approval cases (PUBLISH_REQUEST / CARD_REVISION) and the gate a listing passes before it publishes.
Model settings, dimensions and their values, category rules, rules and their conditions, the simulator.
Quotes priced by the model and moved through their statuses.
Rate cards: draft, entries, submit, approve, reject, archive, revise; the impact read and the dry run over a draft grid.
Surge events, the scraper sources that feed them and the job that runs the due ones.
Media types, size classes, materials, venue types, the match log and the proposals.
A print job on an order and the cost approval that pays the partner.

Lot N: the print partner's KYC on three paths — the partner's own documents or Digio session from the phone, the desk recording it on their behalf, the desk requesting it (Digio on their behalf, or by hand) — reviewed per document on the same workbench as the publisher's and the advertiser's; purged and escalated with them.
Print partners: created, edited, deactivated, reactivated, activated for the app; their ledger, rate card and quote history.
The agent's publisher book.
The publisher's home: dashboard figures and their listings.
Publisher KYC: submitted by the party, reviewed per document from the queue, re-uploads asked, assignment as a filter.
Lot D (Q86): the legacy-book import with its per-row report, commit and revoke.
Publisher accounts: register, the party's own read and edit, the QR grant to an agent, onboarding completion or cancellation, the console directory.
Publishers see the advertiser's per-spot figures on their bookings (Q9): kept present, off until there is data.
K-B1: the console's QR desk — every code with what it names and its scans, one person's scans, regenerate and deactivate with a reason.
Lot G (Q129/Q143): the twelve reports defined in code — run on demand or on a schedule, mailed as a time-limited link.
Commission rates by category or media type, publisher subscriptions and per-publisher overrides.
The fee schedule and the tax settings.
The checkout quote and the price lock that holds it while the advertiser pays.
Publisher subscription plans: the priced catalogue and its editor, self-service orders paid from the wallet, the phone's subscription screen, and the daily expiry sweep.
Safety alerts raised by an agent and worked by ops.
Fraud cases: notes, evidence, the score and its signals, a decision that applies or lifts suspension scopes.
Suspend and reinstate a listing, publisher, advertiser or agent by scope; the read of what is in force.
Ownership claims on a listing, decided by ops.
Compliance cases, the enforcement sweep and the earnings holds it raises.
The supply-side funnel: publishers by stage.
An agent's on-site listing attempt, the acceptances it collects, and the supply root.
Listing documents and site verifications, reviewed from the verification queue.
Disputes: raised, messaged, evidenced, resolved, reopened, rated; the credit release.
Live chat for paid subscribers: the entitlement read, the SSE thread, operator presence and auto-assignment, the desk inbox, canned replies and the first-response sweep.
Support tickets: raised on the phone, queued, replied to, assigned and closed on the console.
The force-update / maintenance gate both apps read before sign-in, and the wizard limits.
The activity log, per target and as a CSV export.
Settings -> Feature flags: every feature across the surfaces, the kill switch, variants, rollback and rollout; the per-caller read the apps boot with.
The enums and flow definitions the apps boot from, edited by the console's flow editor (Q83/Q148).
System health: last dump, last drill, retention-due, job heartbeats; the restore drill and the retention sweep.
Identifier formats per party, the preview, and the publisher backfill.
The integrations row: SMS rails, email, HRMS, work tool, KYC provider mode, maps, audience vendors, the QR engine (QR-1: Local or GenQR, with its connection test) — secrets masked on the way out.
The platform settings row: SLAs, floors, retention windows.
Role configs, their permission lists and their members; the capability matrix the console draws.
Lot G (Q130): the public status page — samples every five minutes, the incident log, regions, and the subscribe / confirm / unsubscribe links.
Inviting a console user by email, resending and withdrawing the invite.

Lot K2: the console's own operators — role, the second factor the next sign-in asks for, last sign-in, state; change role, reset 2FA, invite and create an admin. The app itself is auth.authenticator-app.
K-B1: the contacts beside the primary pair — add, label, prove with a code, make one the primary; the desk does the same with a reason.
Q125: a person's data exported on request (DataExportRequest) — built by the job, released as a time-limited file.
The console's user directory: list, create, edit, delete, reset password and 2FA, bootstrap the first admin.
Read the platform as a party sees it — a 15-minute read-only token, listed and ended here.
A person's own account: profile, party choice, onboarding manifest, preferences, activity, email resubscribe.
DR 07: the devices signed in, and signing them out one by one or all at once.
Issues raised on a project or a task, by severity; an OPEN CRITICAL one flags the task as blocked on read.
A person's own tasks — assigned or reviewing — with their own moves: start, submit for review, block with a reason, comment, log hours, review.
A department's or a city's project: the frame a set of tasks and issues sit in, with counts and an archive.
The DR 10 Tasks section on real tables: tasks with sub-tasks, people, reviewers, prerequisites, comments and hours; the status rules, the board, the overview and the daily due notices.
